passage: Transportation engineers are exploring ways to modernize traffic systems as urban congestion increases. One promising development is the implementation of adaptive traffic signals, which use sensors to monitor real-time conditions at intersections. Unlike traditional signals that operate on fixed timers, adaptive systems adjust the length of green and red lights based on vehicle flow. This approach reduces unnecessary idling, improves travel times, and helps decrease fuel consumption. Early trials have shown notable improvements, particularly during peak commuting hours. However, widespread adoption has been slow. Installing these systems requires upgraded infrastructure, and some cities face budget constraints that delay implementation. Engineers remain optimistic that continued advancements in sensor technology and data processing will eventually make adaptive traffic systems more accessible, leading to smoother and more efficient urban transportation networks.

questions.explanation: Adaptive signals respond to real-time conditions, improving travel, but adoption lags due to infrastructure costs.
